questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to cook with less oil and sugar
How much salt people eat and why too much is harmful
The long history of salt as a valuable product traded around the world
Why processed food is becoming cheaper
questions.why: Neil says they'll be asking “how much salt is too much?” and explains the health risks.

questions.q: What does the WHO recommend as a daily salt intake?
options: Less than 5g, about a teaspoon
At least 1g, the minimum to survive
Around 6g, like in Australia
About 17g for active adults
questions.why: Neil says the WHO recommends less than 5g a day, about the same as a teaspoon.

questions.q: How much salt do people in Kazakhstan eat on average?
options: Exactly the amount the WHO recommends
Slightly less than people in Britain
About twice the recommended amount
Over three times the WHO amount
questions.why: They eat about 17g a day, which is more than three times the WHO amount.

questions.q: Why does Marian mention dairy products?
options: To show that even milk foods were salted to keep them
To explain that Kazakhs rarely eat meat
To suggest dairy is a healthy alternative to salt
To say that dairy products are the saltiest foods in the whole world
questions.why: She says dairy products are also very salty “for the same reasons” – salt preserved food.

questions.q: According to Georgie, what happens when we eat too much salt?
options: The body loses water and becomes dry
The stomach stops digesting food properly and the body feels weak
The body keeps water, so the heart has to work harder
Our sense of taste slowly disappears
questions.why: The body retains water to dilute the salt, so the heart works harder, causing high blood pressure.

questions.q: What has the British government done about salt?
options: Raised its recommended intake to 6g
Banned food companies from adding any salt to processed food
Made laws forcing food companies to use less salt
Put a special tax on salty snacks
questions.why: Neil says Britain passed laws forcing food companies to reduce the salt they use.

questions.q: What is Professor Clare Collins' view?
options: Australia's 6g limit is clearly better than 5g
Salt is only a problem in a few countries
Every country should follow exactly the same rules
Arguing over 5g or 6g misses the bigger problem
questions.why: She says to look at the bigger picture instead of arguing whether it should be 5g or 6g.

questions.q: What does Neil suggest for people who don't like unsalted food?
options: Eat more processed food instead
Add herbs and spices
Use salt only at breakfast
Drink more water with meals
questions.why: He says, “try adding herbs and spices instead.”
